# The Unseen Hand That Set the Stars

## Scripture
"He determines the number of the stars and calls them each by name." — Psalm 147:4

## Reflection

Tonight, if you find a dark enough place, look up. The stars seem countless—scattered like scattered seed across an infinite field. Yet the psalmist tells us something staggering: God doesn't just know the stars exist. He *numbers* them. He calls each one by name.

Think about that for a moment. The nearest star beyond our sun is over four light-years away. Our galaxy alone contains hundreds of billions of stars. And beyond that, billions of other galaxies, each with their own countless suns. This is not a casual inventory. This is intimate, personal attention to every single point of light in the vast darkness.

And if the God who holds the universe in such precise care takes the time to name each star—how much more does He know you? The One who never loses a star in the cosmic deep will never lose sight of you in your struggles, your quiet doubts, or your ordinary days. You are not a nameless speck. You are a called-by-name child of the God who numbers the heavens.

When you feel lost in the immensity of life, remember: the same hand that set Arcturus in its place and named every star in the Milky Way has also written your name on His heart.

## Prayer

Father, You who named the stars before they shone, You know me completely. When I feel tiny and forgotten, remind me that You call me by name. Teach me to trust Your attention to every detail of my life, even as You govern galaxies. Amen.
